clue.text: Miss Jones's personal capital

parts.note: Bridget Jones is the single heroine of Helen Fielding's diary novels
something personal is one's own

explanation.surface: A remark about a woman's own pet city or private fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money belonging to Miss Jones; it is a capital city. BRIDGETOWN is the capital of Barbados.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridgetown is the capital city of Barbados, an example of a capital.

clue.text: Divers in US city losing it surfacing underneath idiot

indicators.note: underneath places the turned city below the idiot in this down light

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: surfacing in a down answer means the letters rise, so they read from bottom to top
losing says the following word's letters drop out of the city

parts.note: Detroit is the Michigan car city
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tale of divers in an American city coming up to the surface beneath a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' reads as people who dive, but it is the old adjective meaning various. DETROIT less IT is DETRO; 'surfacing' turns it upward to ORTED, placed 'underneath' ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers is an old adjective meaning several of various kinds, a synonym of mixed or varied.

clue.text: President Clinton primarily a poor poet and author

parts.note: Harry Truman was the 33rd US president

indicators.note: primarily means only the opening letter of Clinton is used

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: poor signals the letters of poet are in bad shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict that Bill Clinton was chiefly a poor poet and writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'President Clinton' reads as one person, but the president is a different one and Clinton gives only his initial. 'poor' rearranges the poet into POTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Truman Capote was the American writer of In Cold Blood and Breakfast at Tiffany's.

clue.text: Castle engaged in battle, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is heard rather than written, a sound-alike

parts.note: to have engaged in battle is to have fought

explanation.surface: A castle was the scene of combat, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent FOUGHT and FORT sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A fort is a fortified military stronghold, a close synonym of castle.

clue.text: Drunkenness can be cruel, if bishop parking convertible

indicators.note: a convertible can be changed in form, so these letters are rearranged
if here sets a condition: the bishop's letter is taken out and the parking letter stands in its place

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to be worked on
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A warning that drink makes people cruel, even a bishop parking his convertible car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if bishop parking' means P takes B's place in CANBECRUEL, giving CANPECRUEL, which 'convertible' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Crapulence is a formal word for sickness from excessive drinking, intoxication or its after-effects.

clue.text: Red pig almost gobbles one up

indicators.note: up in a down light means the whole lot reads from bottom to top
gobbles means the cut pig swallows the next piece inside it
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the Landrace is a breed of domestic pig
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A red-coated pig nearly wolfs down a single thing.
explanation.walkthrough: LANDRACE less its last letter is LANDRAC; 'gobbles' puts I inside to give LANIDRAC, which 'up' turns to read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal is a deep scarlet colour, named from the robes of cardinals, so a shade of red.

clue.text: See 3
Berserk, then PM not good enough?

parts.note: not p.m. but a.m., the morning half of the day
OK means acceptable, good enough

explanation.surface: A frantic question asking whether the prime minister is up to the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM' looks like the Prime Minister, but it is post meridiem; its opposite is AM.
explanation.definitionFit: To run amok is to go wild in a frenzy, exactly what berserk describes.

clue.text: Lake on small river rippling round duck

parts.note: re means on the subject of
S is the clothing abbreviation for small

indicators.note: round means the rearranged river surrounds the next piece
rippling water is disturbed, so the letters of river are rearranged

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, an O

explanation.surface: A lake fed by a little river with water rippling around a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rippling' gives ERVIR and 'round' wraps it about the duck. A duck is cricket's score of zero, so O.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservoir is an artificial lake used to store water for supply.

clue.text: See 16
Downtrodden wimp?

parts.note: a feeble person everyone walks over, and also a mat that is literally trodden down by feet at the entrance

explanation.definitionFit: A doormat is figuratively a submissive person who lets others treat them badly.

clue.text: Field cut alongside home

indicators.note: alongside means the two pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: pad is slang for one's home or flat
to dock is to cut short, as a tail

explanation.surface: A field has been trimmed next to a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddock is a small enclosed field, typically for horses.

clue.text: Ben, not half socialist, from the right

indicators.note: from the right means the run is read right to left
half takes just the opening two of the four letters

parts.note: the political left is socialist

explanation.surface: Ben, a man who is only half a left-winger, as seen by the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'socialist' fits Ben Elton the left-wing comedian, but gives LEFT, halved to LE. NOT plus LE, read 'from the right', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Elton is the English comedian and writer, so his surname follows Ben.

clue.text: Offer true love madly, gripping pole

indicators.note: gripping means the rearranged letters clasp the next piece inside
madly says the letters are jumbled wildly

parts.note: taken as written as the anagram letters
N is the North Pole's abbreviation

explanation.surface: A passionate suitor declares true love while clutching a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' rearranges TRUELOVE into VOLUTEER; 'gripping' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To volunteer is to offer oneself or one's services freely, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Does vanity put right unpleasant picture?

indicators.note: putting something right reorders it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks whether conceit corrects an ugly image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put right' rearranges the ten letters of DOESVANITY.
explanation.definitionFit: A video nasty is a violent or horrific film on video, an unpleasant picture.

clue.text: Bank about to lend out in evocative manner

indicators.note: about means the bank word goes around the next piece

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on

indicators.note: out signals the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written as the anagram letters

explanation.surface: A bank is on the point of lending money out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like a lender; it is the verb, as in bank on, RELY. 'out' turns TOLEND into DOLENT, which RELY goes 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Redolent means strongly suggestive or reminiscent, so redolently is evocatively.

clue.text: Eminem is on, oddly, after this song?

definitions.text: Eminem is on, oddly, after this song?

parts.words: Eminem is on, oddly, after this song?
parts.note: the odd letters of Eminem is on spell the farmyard refrain that follows the title of a famous nursery song

explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters E, I, E, I, O are the chorus that follows this song's title line.
explanation.definitionFit: This children's song's title line is followed by the refrain ee-i-ee-i-o.

clue.text: Wrong way to wrap new present in unspecific place

indicators.note: to wrap means the jumbled letters go around the next piece
wrong signals the letters are set out incorrectly

parts.note: taken as written as the anagram letters
present means here, in attendance

explanation.surface: Wrapping a gift badly before handing it over somewhere vague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' gives AYW, which 'to wrap' puts around N. 'present' looks like a gift but means in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: Anywhere means in any place at all, an unspecified location.

clue.text: Famous record topped in performance of choir

indicators.note: in means the cut record goes inside the rearranged letters
a performance of something works it over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as the anagram letters

indicators.note: topped means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a list is a written record

explanation.surface: A celebrated recording comes out on top in a choir's concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped' removes the record's first letter; 'performance of' rearranges the choir to H...ORIC so 'in' can set the record inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic means famous or important in history, a notable sense of celebrated.

clue.text: Might the military patrol this area in crotchless pants?

definitions.text: Might the military patrol this area in crotchless pants?

parts.words: Might the military patrol this area in crotchless pants?
parts.note: a zone of airspace banned to aircraft, policed by the military, and also the front area of trousers lacking a fly

explanation.definitionFit: A no-fly zone is airspace where flights are prohibited, enforced by military patrols.

clue.text: Vessel to fit inside dish

indicators.note: inside means the fitting word sits within the dish

parts.note: a flan is an open tart, a dish
to go somewhere is to fit there, as a key that will go in a lock

explanation.surface: Instructions for a vessel to slot inside a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large vessel for wine or ale, with a handle and spout.

clue.text: Fibre in cereals is a lot

indicators.note: in means the answer sits within the following words

explanation.surface: Cereals contain a great deal of dietary fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across cereaLS IS A Lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a stiff plant fibre from agave leaves, used for rope and matting.

clue.text: Leg held by girl lying down, face up

indicators.note: held by means the leg goes inside the girl's name

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name
pins is slang for legs, so one is a pin

explanation.surface: A girl's leg is held as she lies on her back.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine means lying flat on the back, facing upward.

clue.text: Girl virtually man given a tube

indicators.note: virtually means nearly all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Tracy is a girl's name
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A girl who is almost a man gets handed a pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtually' trims the girl's last letter; 'given' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea is the windpipe, the tube carrying air to the lungs.

clue.text: Argument tense, blowing top

indicators.note: blowing its top means losing its first letter

parts.note: stiff means rigid and tense

explanation.surface: A tense quarrel where someone loses their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing top' looks like losing one's temper; here it drops the S of STIFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a petty quarrel, a minor argument.

clue.text: Spooner sees "Starsky and Hutch Investigate Lustful Lucy", a cinema favourite

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: Starsky and Hutch were TV detectives in a cop show
a film about lustful Lucy would be porn

explanation.surface: An imagined film title of TV detectives probing a lascivious woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The pretend title is cop porn; swapping the opening C and P gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Popcorn is the classic snack eaten at the cinema.

clue.text: Formal choice seen shortly

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: prime means choice, of top quality

explanation.surface: A formal choice will be seen soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' looks like soon; it cuts PRIME short.
explanation.definitionFit: Prim means stiffly formal and proper.

clue.text: Left in top, back to bottom

indicators.note: back means the whole run is read in reverse
in means the letter for left is put inside the top

parts.note: a roof is the top of a building

explanation.surface: Something left at the top is moved back down to the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside ROOF to make ROOLF; 'back' reverses it. Roof to floor is top to bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The floor is the bottom surface of a room.

clue.text: In a cycle test, nine failed to enter

indicators.note: to enter means the jumbled letters go inside the test word

parts.note: a trial is a test

indicators.note: failed suggests the letters have broken down and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as the anagram letters

explanation.surface: A cycling test that nine riders failed to take part in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failed' gives ENNI, which goes 'to enter' the test between TRI and AL. 'cycle' tempts toward bikes, but the definition is about recurring periods.
explanation.definitionFit: Triennial means recurring every three years, so occurring in a regular cycle.
